task_details.trap: clinical data (the diagnosis) is out of scope for billing settlement
task_details.trap_rationale: a hospital policy choice, not the Act's: insurer and TPA claims in India routinely carry ICD-coded diagnoses, but that is claims adjudication -- a separate purpose this policy does not model. Reconciling an invoice with a payment needs no diagnosis.

rationale.patient_administration/mrn: the record the patient is registered under
rationale.patient_administration/date_of_birth: disambiguates a match against an existing record
rationale.patient_administration/phone: how to reach them about the visit

task_details.trap: financial data (the policy number, cover) is out of scope for registration
task_details.trap_rationale: a hospital policy choice, not the Act's: many front desks capture TPA or insurer details for cashless admission. This policy keeps cover with billing, so registration -- identifying the person and booking the visit -- does not take it.

rationale.patient_administration/mrn: identifies the patient for the ward round
rationale.patient_administration/date_of_birth: age, stated on a clinical summary
rationale.clinical_ehr/mrn: joins this module's rows to the patient -- without it the export cannot say whose they are

task_details.trap: an onward use (the research registry) beyond the specified purpose
task_details.trap_rationale: an onward use beyond the specified purpose: a research registry is a separate purpose with its own basis (the Act's research exemption has conditions), never a side-effect of care.

rationale.patient_administration/mrn: identifies the patient for the consultant
rationale.clinical_ehr/mrn: joins this module's rows to the patient -- without it the export cannot say whose they are

task_details.trap: retention of a year exceeds care coordination's 90-day ceiling
task_details.trap_rationale: the purpose's retention ceiling (90 days, the hospital's policy for a care extract -- not the source medical record, which is kept far longer) is exceeded by a year on file.

register_evidence: demonstrated by the pipeline (evidence produced per run):
TLS              the browser reads the TLS session of the connection it made (protocol, issuer, validity: HISDataSource.transport_secure); a manifest claiming TLS over http is unsubstantiated
PSEUDO-EXPORT    interop.normalise.audit searches the written export for every raw identifier pulled
PURGE-01         compliance.retention: every export carries a delete-after sidecar; purge_expired erases and logs
AUDIT-LOG        compliance.audit: the harness writes an event per run at the metering boundary, with the fields pulled and a digest of the manifest declared
ROPA             compliance.processing_record: the record is generated from the audit log, per purpose, so it cannot fall behind what ran
AUTH-RPA-2026    the portal adapter refuses a portal whose robots.txt disallows it unless this reference is given, and the harness writes it and the account into every audit event
attested by the deployment (on the register; not produced by this code):
ENC-REST         extracted store encrypted at rest
ACL-STORE        role-based access control on the extracted store
NOTICE-REG-2026  patient privacy notice, acknowledged at registration
LU-CARE          legitimate use -- the purpose for which the patient provided her data: provision of medical services
LU-BILL          legitimate use -- the purpose for which the patient provided her data: settlement of amounts due for services provided
LU-REG           legitimate use -- the purpose for which the patient provided her data: registration and scheduling for provision of services

note: ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, NOTICE-REG-2026 and DPO describe the hospital's production store and governance; the demo writes its exports as plain files under data/ with no ACL, so they are not true of the demo machine
